articles.standfirst: El campeón del mundo de F1 ha comprado una nave para iniciar una colección de coches: y los primeros que menciona son espectaculares
articles.summary: El campeón del mundo de F1 ha comprado una nave para iniciar una colección de coches: y los primeros que menciona son espectaculares
articles.body: Andrea Kimi Antonelli es la nueva joya de Mercedes, ahora ya coronado como flamante campeón del mundo de Fórmula 1, el más joven de la historia en conseguirlo. Un logro que merece, sin duda, un capricho. Y el jovencísimo boloñés (de 20 años) tiene claro cuál es: quiere regalarse una colección de coches. De momento sólo tiene uno, su 'coche de empresa', el Mercedes-AMG GT63, al que cuida con tanto mimo que confesó lavarlo a mano él mismo antes de partir para cada Gran Premio. Pero no va a ser el último, aunque a sus padres no les guste mucho la idea. "Le damos una paga mensual, porque si no se lo gastaría todo en coches", confesaba su padre, Marco, hace apenas unas semanas, revelando así una de las grandes pasiones de la nueva estrella de la Fórmula 1. Sin embargo, parece que sus progenitores no van a poder frenar durante mucho más tiempo el ímpetu de su vástago. En una entrevista con Auto Motor und Sport, el joven campeón del mundo revela sus planes. De momento, ha comprado ya una nave en la que dar cobijo a sus próximas adquisiciones: "Algún día me gustaría tener una gran flota de coches, pero primero quería pensar dónde guardarlos y traerlos uno a uno. Me gustan los modelos más modernos y futuristas, pero también los icónicos que han hecho historia". Antonelli tiene bastante claro cuáles le llaman más la atención... y demuestra buen gusto para los coches cuando se le pregunta por cuáles serían sus elecciones: "Me encanta el 300 SL Gullwing [el mítico 'Alas de Gaviota']. Por supuesto, en plata. Y me gusta mucho el Mercedes CLK en su versión de carretera de Le Mans [el CLK GTR]. Es realmente precioso". Curiosamente, coincide en preferencias con Fernando Alonso, quien ya posee uno de ellos. Otro que está en el radar del campeón es el Mercedes-AMG CLE 646, una serie limitada de sólo 30 piezas que, además, se presentó por primera vez en los prolegómenos del Gran Premio de España, en Madring, con la presencia del propio Antonelli y de su compañero George Russell.

articles.title: Inside CM Punk's life away from wrestling: How his difficult childhood, family struggles, marriage to AJ Lee, and journey toward happiness shaped his WWE life
articles.summary: Explore CM Punk's life journey beyond wrestling, including his difficult childhood, straight-edge philosophy, marriage to AJ Lee, and new ventures after WWE, revealing his pursuit of happiness and personal growth.
articles.body: CM Punk, AKA Phillip Jack Brooks, has had a life full of defining moments, inside and outside the wrestling ring. His legacy is etched in stone with his successes in WWE and other wrestling promotions, but his personal life has been a path of difficult family relationships, professional challenges, and efforts to find contentment outside the world of wrestling.CM Punk was born in Chicago, Illinois, and raised in Lockport, developing an independent outlook at an early age. His upbringing affected his lifestyle choices, especially his choice of the straight-edge philosophy. His relationship with AJ Lee over the years, his interests outside of wrestling, and his willingness to step away from the spotlight all of these things have provided a different perspective on his life.How CM Punk's difficult childhood shaped his straight-edge identity and personal life beyond WWECM Punk was born on October 26, 1978, in Chicago, Illinois. Growing up in a difficult home affected some of his personal decisions. His father battled alcoholism, which reportedly factored into Punk’s decision to reject alcohol and drugs.In his teens he went straight-edge, giving up alcohol, recreational drugs and tobacco. This philosophy became a defining part of his identity and would later influence his public persona in professional wrestling.Punk also got into punk rock music, comic books, and professional wrestling early. He worked at All American Comics in Evergreen Park, Illinois, while trying to break into the business on the independent wrestling circuit before becoming a major name in the WWE.His upbringing was not easy. He has been reported to have had troubled relationships with members of his family, including his mother and older brother. These personal struggles led to a complex relationship with his history and helped form the independent character that audiences would eventually know.CM Punk explored new paths after leaving WWECM Punk’s personal life changed dramatically when he began dating fellow WWE performer April Mendez, better known to the world as AJ Lee. The duo is said to have started dating in 2013 and tied the knot on June 13, 2014, in a private ceremony.Their relationship became part of Punk’s life, especially during uncertain times in his professional wrestling career. In a 2026 interview with Stephanie McMahon, Punk got personal about his upbringing and admitted that popping the question to April was scarier than fighting in the UFC or wrestling at WrestleMania. He also described their relationship as the most important thing in his life.Punk and Lee both grew up in difficult families, and they understand each other’s personal problems. Lee has also spoken publicly about her childhood experiences and mental health, including financial struggles and her family's history of mental illness.They’ve kept their lives pretty private outside of wrestling. Their relationship has remained an important part of their lives, despite the demands of their respective careers and occasional returns to WWE.CM Punk’s Post WWE AdventuresCM Punk’s exit from WWE in 2014 was such a huge turning point in his professional and personal life. After years of traveling, performing, and dealing with physical injuries, he stepped away from the wrestling industry to explore opportunities outside the ring.He was interested in mixed martial arts, acting, comic-book writing, and sports commentary. He signed with the Ultimate Fighting Championship in 2014 and fought two professional MMA fights. Neither fight ended in a win, but the experience enabled him to pursue a dream beyond professional wrestling.Punk also pursued his love of entertainment in the fields of acting and comic books. He showed up in the horror movie Girl on the Third Floor and worked on Marvel’s Drax comic series. These opportunities enabled him to explore interests that existed long before his wrestling fame.In a 2026 interview with Stephanie McMahon, Punk reflected on his mindset and how his childhood and personal relationships played into that. His journey shows that life outside the wrestling ring has been more than just championship wins, with family, personal development and finding a balance between professional ambitions still important chapters of his story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Playlist: Fantasy basketball waiver-wire adds and schedule breakdown for Week 6
articles.summary: Dan Titus takes you through his top waiver wire adds and schedule breakdown for Week 6 of fantasy basketball.
articles.body:
Happy Thanksgiving week! There are no games Thursday, and it's a tough week to stream, with only two days — Tuesday (three games) and Saturday (five) — with fewer than nine games on the slate. There's some good news on the injury front: Brandon Ingram is back and set to make his Clippers debut Monday against Houston, and we should see Austin Reaves (heel) return for the Lakers as well. On the other side, we lost Evan Mobley to a toe injury and Dylan Harper to a hip injury.

Every league is different, so I'm focusing on players who are under 50% rostered on Yahoo.

Tuesday features three games, while Saturday has five. The Magic and Wizards are the only teams playing on both slates, so streaming from them is my priority given the circumstances in Week 6.

Tristan da Silva, SF/PF, Orlando Magic (20% rostered)

Da Silva is my top Tuesday-and-Saturday pickup. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) still out, he's playing 29.9 minutes per game and averaging 13.8 points and 3.2 3s on the season, and he scored 18 points with 4 3s at Washington on Sunday. Orlando has a tough matchup against Detroit, then gets an easier game against Washington on Saturday, the front end of a back-to-back. Add him for points, 3s and low turnovers. He's scored at least 12 points in five of his last six contests.

Bilal Coulibaly, SG/SF, Washington Wizards (7% rostered)

Washington only plays twice, but both games are on the light nights: Tuesday against Boston and Saturday against Orlando. He's a stocks play, averaging 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks in 24.9 minutes this season, with 5.5 rebounds and 1.3 blocks over his last six games. He had 12 points with 3 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 block, 4 3s and 3 turnovers Sunday against Orlando, so there's at least some recent success to point towards.

Goga Bitadze, C, Orlando Magic (2% rostered)

The backup center for the Magic looks to have passed Nikola Vučević on the depth chart. He's averaging 6.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 0.7 steals and 0.8 blocks on 86% shooting from the field in 18.0 minutes over his last six games. He won't wow you by any means, but extra boards and a strong FG% can help in 9-cat. Feel free to ignore if you're in a points league.

Shallow league options I'd pick up for Tuesday and Saturday

Kelly Oubre Jr., SF/PF, Indiana Pacers (36% rostered): A top-55 player over the last two weeks in 9-cat, Oubre is producing 15.7 points, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks, with at least 14 points in six straight games. He's worth holding as long as he keeps starting. Indy has a weird schedule, playing on Monday and then a back-to-back on Friday and Saturday.

Cameron Johnson, SF/PF, Denver Nuggets (33% rostered): He's averaging 13.2 points, 1.3 steals and 1.5 3s in 28.8 minutes over his last six games. Johnson plays Tuesday.

Kevin Huerter, SG/SF, Detroit Pistons (25% rostered): He's played 36-plus minutes in four straight with Duncan Robinson (quad) out, and he's been a top-65 player over the last two weeks (15.3 points, 3.7 assists, 1.4 blocks). You can start him on Tuesday and drop him afterward.

Deeper league options I'd pick up for Tuesday and Saturday

Isaac Okoro, SG/SF, Chicago Bulls (10% rostered): Okoro is playing way better as a starter, averaging 10.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.1 steals, and 0.3 blocks in 31.0 minutes over his last eight games. There's no need to rush to get him since you'd only play him on Saturday versus Indy.

Kenrich Williams, PF/C, Oklahoma City Thunder (8% rostered): With so many injuries in OKC's frontcourt, Williams ranks 98th over the past two weeks in 9-cat. He gets steals, doesn't turn over the ball and chips in low-end stats across categories, but nothing to hurt you. Again, you can wait since the only opportunity to stream will be when OKC plays on Saturday.

Brooklyn, Milwaukee and Philadelphia are the only four-game teams with a game on a light night (Saturday). The other six (Clippers, Memphis, Minnesota, Phoenix, Portland and San Antonio) only play on the crowded Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday slates, so in daily leagues you'll have to bench someone for one of these guys. And it could be warranted.

Cam Spencer, PG/SG, Memphis Grizzlies (45% rostered)

Spencer was in my Week 5 rotation and he's still the best multi-week guard I'd grab if he's out there. He had 26 points on 9-of-11 shooting with 5 3s and 7 assists at Cleveland on Wednesday, then dished out 11 assists against Golden State on Thursday. Over the last two weeks, he's at 13.6 points, 6.5 assists and 2.1 3s on 58% shooting, good for top-45 value in 9-cat. Ty Jerome is back so that will lessen his impact. But he remains one of the top backups to hold in fantasy. It hasn't gone unnoticed that the Grizzlies offense is better with Spencer running point over Jerome.

Brayden Burries, SG, Milwaukee Bucks (34% rostered)

The backcourt is a mess, but Burries is another four-game add who can be a multi-week hold. The Bucks are 1-16 through Sunday, so the more losses come, the more we will see the young prospects play. Burries is coming off his best game, scoring 26 points with 8 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 3s in 26 minutes Saturday at Philadelphia. He's been a top-125 player over the last two weeks, averaging 12.5 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.9 assists, and 1.0 steal per game. Milwaukee is one of only three four-game teams that play Saturday, so you'll get something out of him this week, too.

Julian Champagnie, SF/PF, San Antonio Spurs (34% rostered): Champagnie has played 27.6 minutes per game over the last two weeks, averaging 11.0 points and 2.7 3s, with 0.6 steals and 0.6 blocks. If you need 3s and stocks, he can help as the week progresses.

Jaylen Wells, SG/SF/PF, Memphis Grizzlies (21% rostered): Beyond the three-position eligibility, Wells is at 11.9 points and 2.4 3s over his last eight contests. I prefer him for 9-cat formats to take advantage of his efficiency, shooting 48% from the field and 93% from the line over the past two weeks.

Anfernee Simons, PG/SG, Philadelphia 76ers (11% rostered): A points-and-3s play who gets you a Saturday game on a four-game week. He scored 18 in each of his last two games and is at 2.6 3s on 52% shooting over his last seven.

Egor Dëmin, PG/SG, Brooklyn Nets (20% rostered): I'm eyeing Saturday's matchup against Charlotte. He's at 14.0 points and 2.4 3s over his last five, but on 39% shooting, and his role expands if Nolan Traoré (hamstring) sits.

Jordan Goodwin, PG/SG, Phoenix Suns (6% rostered): A top-100 player over the last two weeks with 5.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.2 steals in 22.3 minutes.

4 games (9) : Brooklyn, the Clippers, Memphis, Milwaukee, Minnesota, Philadelphia, Phoenix, Portland and San Antonio.

Best streaming spots : Brooklyn, Milwaukee and Philadelphia are the only four-game teams with a game on a light night (Saturday). No four-game team plays Tuesday.

Tuesday (3 games): Boston, Dallas, Denver, Detroit, Orlando and Washington.

Saturday (5 games): Brooklyn, Charlotte, Chicago, Houston, Indiana, Milwaukee, Oklahoma City, Orlando, Philadelphia and Washington.

Both: Orlando and Washington. Washington only plays twice, but both games are on light nights, so a Wizard can be useful in daily leagues even on a two-game week.

Teams to avoid for streaming (barring notable injuries)

2 games (3) : Atlanta. The Hawks don't play until Friday against the Celtics and Sunday versus the Knicks. If you want to add Kingston Flemings or Aaron Wiggins before the weekend, I'd buy that.

Dallas plays on Tuesday and Friday, so dropping fringe assets like Naji Marshall and others makes sense.

articles.title: Egoitz Bijueska se rompe la clavícula
articles.standfirst: Sufrió una caída el último día de grabaciones en un evento con Monster Energy
articles.summary: Sufrió una caída el último día de grabaciones en un evento con Monster Energy
articles.body: Egoitz Bijueska se rompió la clavícula izquierda. El skater español lo ha anunciado en su cuenta de Instagram. Acompaña el mensaje con una radiografía de cómo ha quedado su articulación tras la caída sufrida en el skatepark. Bijueska, que reeditó su corona de campeón mundial de parl en octubre durante los World Games en Asunción (Paraguay), se encontraba en un Tour con el equipo internacional de Monster Energy. Había participado en varias grabaciones con esta marca hasta que el último día se cayó y se rompió la clavícula. Egoitz, que este martes 24 de noviembre cumplirá 16 años, está ahora de vuelta a Bilbao. "¡Qué viaje tan enfermizo! Me rompí la clavícula en el último día. ¡Pero aún así fue una semana muy divertida!", escribió el actual número 1 del ranking mundial en park. Hace dos meses, en una entrevista en MARCA, apuntaba que en un futuro se veía siendo pro del skate en Estados Unidos, viviendo por allí y que sueña con ganar en los Juegos Olímpicos. Este 2026 logró ganar dos Mundiales en un intervalo de meses. Se proclamó campeón del World Skate en Río de Janeiro en marzo y repitió corona en los World Skate Games de octubre. Entremedias, se colgó el oro en los X-Games, por delante del estadounidenese Tom Schaar y el australiano Keegan Palmer, que fueron subcampeón y campeón respectivamente, en los Juegos de París 2024.

articles.title: 'FIFA World Cup has standard 90-minute game': India's R Praggnanandhaa questions changing chess time controls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa has sparked a fresh debate, advocating for a single, uniform classical time control across the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa has sparked a fresh debate, advocating for a single, uniform classical time control across the entire World Championship cycle.Taking to X on Monday following the conclusion of the Total Chess Pilot event, the Indian prodigy argued that constantly shifting between different game durations makes it harder for both competitors to prepare and spectators to follow the sport."After the Total Chess event, I started thinking more about the World Championship cycle format," Praggnanandhaa wrote. "One thing I've been wondering about is the time control. I feel rather than having 4 different time controls throughout the cycle, it would be better to have one classical time control and use it consistently in every event."The recent Total Chess pilot event used a 45+30 fast classical time control. Major FIDE qualifying tournaments and World Championship matches currently follow different formats, with game durations ranging from shorter classical sessions to marathon seven-hour encounters.Praggnanandhaa believes adopting a single, standardised time control across the entire World Championship cycle would bring greater consistency and make the sport easier to follow for both players and fans."Whether it's 45+30, 90 mins + 40 moves or the 7-hour format used in the Grand Swiss, having consistency could be good for both players and fans," he added.The Grandmaster also raised concerns over reported changes to the upcoming 2027 FIDE World Cup, which is set to split its classical time controls between stages.Drawing a parallel with global football, he questioned the logic of changing the fundamental rhythm of a tournament midway through."I also read that the new World Cup 2027 format will have 45+30 in the Group Stage and 90 mins + 40 moves in the Knockouts. I feel these are two completely different formats," Praggnanandhaa noted. "To give an example, the FIFA World Cup has a standard 90-minute game, and it doesn't change for qualifiers, the Group Stage or the Knockouts."Highlighting the viewer experience alongside competitive fairness, he explained that predictable match lengths help audiences engage better with broadcasts."I feel having one consistent time control would make it easier for fans to follow the games and plan their day around them," he said. "As a player, I would personally prefer to have one classical time control throughout the World Championship cycle, as it would allow us to adapt to and focus on one classical time control."Clarifying that his post was meant to encourage constructive dialogue, Praggnanandhaa concluded, "P.S. This is just to start a discussion on the topic. I haven't read anything specific about this, and these are just my personal thoughts."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc’s Ferrari rivalry takes another turn as Martin Brundle’s Las Vegas GP prediction comes true
articles.summary: Martin Brundle’s warning about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc has become a reality after the Ferrari teammates collided during the Las Vegas Grand
articles.body: Martin Brundle’s warning about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc has become a reality after the Ferrari teammates collided during the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The incident happened despite Ferrari having held talks with both drivers following their earlier disagreement at the Mexico Grand Prix. Charles Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for causing the collision, while Hamilton was left fighting to recover his lost positions.Martin Brundle predicted another Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collision after Mexico GPThe latest incident was not entirely unexpected for former Formula 1 driver and Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle. After Hamilton and Leclerc’s controversial encounter at the Mexico Grand Prix, Ferrari made it clear that the two drivers had discussed their differences and were ready to move forward.However, Brundle was not convinced that one conversation would prevent another disagreement on the track. Speaking to Sky Sports ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, he explained why two teammates could still end up fighting each other, even when they are racing for the same team.Brundle said, “They’re hardwired racing drivers. It’s a curious business we have where you perform as an individual, totally in a team environment. You’re measured as an individual. You’re rewarded as an individual.“Then when the adrenaline is up, and the chance of the gap is there, as the great Ayrton Senna said, ‘If you don’t go for a gap, you’re no longer a racing driver,’ and that’s what they did.”He also pointed out that Leclerc had experienced frustration during the season and explained how such incidents could affect everyone working behind the scenes.“There’s some frustration. Charles had some frustrations this year, so it doesn’t look pretty for the team. It’s like when Lando Norris ran into Oscar Piastri in Singapore in the sprint race. It doesn’t look pretty for the team, and you’ve let 1,500 people down, and that’s just the car side without the power unit side, and you’ve let people down in your team.”Brundle believed Ferrari would speak to both drivers again, but he had doubts about whether the same problem could be avoided in future races.Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collide again as Ferrari receives another setback at Las Vegas GPThe Las Vegas Grand Prix gave Ferrari another reason to worry about its drivers. Both Hamilton and Leclerc had a difficult qualifying session, with neither making it into Q3. They started outside the top 10 but managed to move up the order during the race.However, their progress took a turn when they came together at Turn 7. Hamilton was trying to get past Oscar Piastri, while Leclerc also attempted to pass his teammate from the inside. The Monegasque driver made contact with Hamilton’s car, sending the seven-time world champion into a spin and costing him several positions.The FIA stewards investigated the incident and held Leclerc responsible. According to the official FIA decision, Leclerc had started his overtaking move from too far behind and did not have the right to claim the inside line at the corner. He was handed a 10-second time penalty.Hamilton eventually finished seventh, while Leclerc dropped to 10th after the penalty.The reaction from Ferrari’s management showed how serious the situation had become. Team principal Fred Vasseur called the incident unacceptable, particularly because the team had already spoken to both drivers after their Mexico clash.Hamilton also avoided discussing the incident in detail, saying it was something Ferrari needed to handle internally. Leclerc, meanwhile, accepted responsibility for the collision and admitted that he felt embarrassed for the team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: WWE star Cody Rhodes reveals unique strategy he would adopt if he decides to enter a potential political career
articles.summary: WWE star Cody Rhodes has not been shy about admitting his interest in politics and his desire to potentially become a politician one day, and the WWE star
articles.body: WWE star Cody Rhodes has not been shy about admitting his interest in politics and his desire to potentially become a politician one day, and the WWE star has a strategy that he believes could work in today's political climate. He has recently opened up about his potential political ambitions, revealing an unusual strategy that he would pick up if he ever decides to enter politics.The Undisputed Champion believes that taking a more positive approach towards political opponents could help him stand out in an increasingly divisive political environment. Rhodes has expressed interest in becoming a politician in Georgia over the last few years, discussed the possibility during an appearance on "The Nikki & Brie Show," and even shared an approach he could take to gain popularity. Let’s take a look at the approach and strategy that he would apply to pursue his potential political career.Undisputed WWE Champion Cody Rhodes discusses his growing interest in joining US politicsWWE superstar Cody Rhodes has opened up about his potential political ambitions. He has particularly revealed the strategy he would adopt if he joins US politics. The Undisputed WWE Champion has noted the polarizing and toxic nature of social media and said that he would take a different approach. He believes that taking a more positive approach would be increasingly divisive.Rhodes discussed the possibility of pursuing a political career during his appearance on The Nikki & Brie Show. The WWE star has criticised the growing hostility surrounding political discussions, particularly on social media.According to Rhodes, political disagreements have increasingly shifted from discussions about policies and governance to personal attacks against candidates. He believes this approach has contributed to a toxic political atmosphere, something he would attempt to avoid if he ever decided to run for public office.The American Nightmare explained that his strategy would involve publicly praising his political opponents rather than engaging in personal attacks against them, "I said if I ever run for any type of office, I'm just going to overly babyface the other candidate. Just, I'm ready. 'Yeah, he said I was terrible, and I had a lisp and all this.' I'm [like], 'This guy's awesome. Lovely. I just think his policy isn't good.'"He further suggested that he would acknowledge positive qualities in his opponents while keeping disagreements focused on their policies rather than their personal lives.Rhodes' comments reflect his frustration with the increasingly polarised nature of political discourse. He believes candidates should be able to disagree over policies without resorting to personal insults or attempting to destroy each other's reputations.The American Nightmare's childhood dream of becoming the President of the United StatesApart from this, Cody Rhodes earlier revealed his childhood dream of becoming a US President. Earlier in 2026, the WWE superstar revealed that he had two major dreams growing up: becoming a professional wrestler like his legendary father, Dusty Rhodes, and becoming the President of the United States. He called the childhood dream a terrible thing. He also highlighted how his prominent neck tattoo could stand in the way of him becoming President.While Rhodes has successfully established himself as one of WWE's biggest superstars, his political ambitions have remained a subject of discussion over the years. Though he has no concrete plan to pursue a political career, his latest comment suggests that the possibility remains a possibility for him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Dylan Larkin has finally been traded to the Montreal Canadiens, and the former Detroit Red Wings center is set to make his debut against the Los Angeles Kings on Monday. He was acquired from the Detroit Red Wings in a blockbuster trade. According to reports, Larkin, who has been waiting long for a trade deal, was acquired from the Detroit Red Wings in a blockbuster trade. Following his acquisition, the former Red wings captain will appear in the lineup at the Bell Centre on November 23.Larkin was seen participating in Montreal's morning skate ahead of the match and will play with jersey No. 89 with his new team. Meanwhile, the Montreal Canadiens general manager has addressed the media following the team's blockbuster acquisition of Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin. The Canadiens officially acquired Larkin from the Red Wings on Sunday night, ending a prolonged trade saga. The deal shows the Montreal Canadiens have established top-six forward as the franchise continues to push towards becoming a Stanley Cup contender.Dylan Larkin to appear against the Los Angeles Kings in debut match with the Montreal CanadiensDylan Larkin will make his debut for the Montreal Canadiens against the Los Angeles Kings at Bell Centre on Monday, one day after he was acquired in a trade with the Detroit Red Wings. Larkin has been looking for opportunities the entire season; however, after a long wait, the Canadiens officially acquired Larkin from the Red Wings on Sunday night.It is important to note that after the 2025-26 season, Larkin requested a trade from Detroit and subsequently lost the captaincy he had held since 2021. He was selected 15th overall in the 2014 NHL Draft. Many teams have been trying to reach out to Larkin. Earlier, the Boston Bruins made an offer for Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin, but the proposal was rejected. However, it is unclear whether Detroit rejected the offer or Larkin did.Speaking about the acquisition, "I think he fits in perfectly. It might take a little bit to get kind of comfortable with it all, but he's a smart hockey player, and he's able to succeed wherever he's at," Canadiens forward Cole Caufield said.In exchange for Larkin, Detroit received forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, and Michael Hage's rights. The players are a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fourth-round pick and a 2029 first-round pick. Montreal also received Detroit's 2028 second-round pick and 2027 third-round pick as part of their transaction.The trade brings an end to his 12-season association with the franchise. He has also scored at least 30 goals in each of the past five seasons, demonstrating his ability to deliver consistent offensive production. As for his perfomance, Larkin has recorded six points, including two goals and four assists, in 10 appearances for Detroit during the 2026-27 campaign before his departure. It is important to note that the forward is also coming off an Olympic gold-medal-winning campaign with the United States at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. He's firmly in the high-end fantasy QB2 mix with low-end QB1 potential given his late season slate.

Watson is also someone worth considering as a fantasy starter this week and beyond.

The Browns have one of the softest schedules the rest of the way, including the Raiders, Bengals, Falcons, Giants, Ravens and Colts. That stretch begins with a Raiders defense that's top-five in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

Cleveland hasn't had many favorable opponents for Watson, but he finished as a top-10 weekly fantasy QB in the two games against easier defenses (Titans in Week 5, Texans in Week 10).

You can expect that to happen at least a few more times given his rushing stats and the Browns' strong, young pass-catching corps of Denzel Boston, KC Conception and Harold Fannin Jr.

Cam Ward is 52% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

Somehow Black remains available in over 50% of Yahoo leagues, despite my endless pleas for managers to stash him on their benches. I'm not including him on the Top-10 pickups list, but just know he would be my top add.

In better matchups, Black has shown solid RB3/flex value while backing up Christian McCaffrey and if the veteran ever misses time we would see Black emerge as a top-10 fantasy option.

If you need a real-life example of what Black could do if CMC were ever sidelined, just look at what happened with Emmett Johnson when Kenneth Walker III sat out the last two weeks. Don't let players with that kind of upside remain on the waiver wire.

Bhayshul Tuten is one of the breakout stars of the 2026 season, but he's missed or been limited in several practices over the last few weeks. To his credit, the sophomore back has managed to suit up every week. Unfortunately, he missed time on Sunday while battling the injuries, leading to just a 43% snap share and 13 touches for 53 scoreless yards in the loss.

If the Jaguars are serious about contending for a Super Bowl, they need their star runner healthy for the stretch run, which makes you wonder if they will ever give him a week off. This week's matchup with the Titans seems like the perfect opportunity to get Tuten some rest, since Jacksonville is 14.5-point favorites.

In that scenario, Rodriguez would step into the lead role and be a potential fantasy RB1 given the opponents and likely positive game script.

Sampson hasn't had the biggest stat lines since returning from injured reserve, but he has been productive with yardage totals 77, 69, 48 and 37 over the last four outings.

More importantly, he out-snapped Quinshon Judkins in three straight outings, turning this backfield into a 50-50 committee.

Without a Judkins injury, the ceiling is limited with Sampson, so keep your expectations in check. But he's definitely worth considering as an RB3/flex option.

Even without Lamar Jackson, Hill has been productive over the last three games. The veteran pass-catcher has at least eight touches in each of those outings, while amassing 92 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 9, 38 yards and five receptions in Week 10, as well as a season-high 98 yards and a TD on Sunday.

Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after the loss to the Panthers, so he should be fine for Week 12 barring any symptoms popping up over the next 24 hours. However, even with Henry starting, we've still seen Hill have a set role in the offense, with the duo splitting snaps fairly evenly over this three-game span.

Jacoby Brissett has given Hill 12 targets during his two starts and that doesn't seem to be going away. Fantasy managers can target Hill as an RB3/flex with some upside thanks to his pass-catching and occasional big plays.

Saquon Barkley appeared to injure his shoulder and potentially suffered his second stinger of the season on Sunday. After the game, Barkley admitted he won't be 100% for the rest of the season, but remained confident he would play Thursday against the Cowboys.

If Barkley is right, then Shipley would only be a flex option thanks to a good matchup with the Cowboys. However, if Barkley ends up being held out on Thanksgiving, Shipley would become one of the top pickups of the week.

Knight hasn't made a huge dent in the box score over the last two games, but it's worth remembering that the Cardinals squared off against two tougher run defenses in the Rams and Chiefs.

The reason I'm mentioning Knight now, is due to the Cardinals' remaining schedule. The Commanders and Eagles are on deck the next two games, followed by a bye in Week 14. Then things get more interesting with the Jets, Saints and Raiders during the fantasy playoffs. Each of those defenses ranks inside the top-10 for most fantasy points allowed to running backs.

If Jeremiyah Love isn't activated from IR, Knight has a chance to produce as a sneaky fantasy option in those matchups.

Kenny Gainwell is 54% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add behind Black and Rodriguez, if available.

It's not a great week for fantasy receivers on the waiver wire, which is why Douglas is leading this section despite only managing 30 yards against the Bills.

The rookie has posted at least 70 yards in four of his seven appearances this season. That includes some very strong volume in the last three weeks, with at least eight targets in each of those outings.

It's hard to trust anyone catching passes from Kyle McCord, but Douglas remains in the WR3/flex mix. However, just like Kaelon Black, I'm going to exclude him from the top-10 pickups since I've highlighted him enough in past weeks.

Hurst's five catches, 56 yards and two touchdowns on seven targets was one of the more shocking outcomes from Week 11. I was high on the rookie prior to the season, but his playing time had dwindled down to just 2% of the snaps in Week 9 and he hadn't caught a pass in any of his last three outings.

Coming out of the bye, the Buccaneers clearly made an effort to emphasize him and his snap share rose to 64% — his highest mark since Week 3.

After the contest, Todd Bowles told reporters the team plans to feature Hurst more moving forward, especially early in games. With Emeka Egbuka disappointing and Chris Godwin Jr. fading, it only makes sense to see what they have in Hurst. This performance puts him in the WR4/flex conversation as a boom-or-bust option.

With Wan'Dale Robinson out for the season, Dike becomes a very intriguing fantasy add in an uptempo Titans' offense that's come to life over the last month.

In the first game with Robinson on IR, Dike led the team in targets (seven) and played the second-most snaps among the receivers behind only Carnell Tate. The result was six receptions and 69 yards with another four yards on the ground. It's his second solid stat line over the last three outings, after he posted a 5-71-1 day in Week 8.

While it might feel odd to invest in the Titans' passing attack, this is a team that's finding its identity as the season progresses. Dike can excel as a playmaker in this environment. He also has a decent schedule coming up with the Jags, Commanders, Lions, Colts and Raiders over the next five weeks.

It's always risky writing about a player who hasn't taken the field yet on the week. Williams will face the Bengals on Monday Night Football, in a likely high-scoring game that should give him every opportunity to put up a nice stat line.

As always, I'll be updating this article after the Monday nighter, so be prepared for Williams to move up or down depending on how he performs.

Prior to Monday night, the rookie had at least 50 yards or a touchdown in three of his last four games since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season. His schedule is also favorable in the coming weeks with the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons. With Stefon Diggs drawing the attention of top corners, Williams could earn more volume during that span.

Mumpfield hasn't taken advantage of the opportunity he's been given this season with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams missing so much time.

Now that Nacua and Terrance Ferguson are done for the season and Adams isn't expected back until mid-December, there is another chance for the 24-year-old wideout to step up. Based on where I have him placed in this column, you can probably tell I'm skeptical. Mumpfield has been held to 20 yards or less and really only popped up for bigger days twice thanks to big plays in those games.

I expect the Rams to lean on their defense, rushing attack and tight ends to grind out wins until Adams returns in a few weeks. But if you're in a deeper format and searching for help at receiver, Mumpfield has a path to production.

articles.title: Jeff Hardy believes WWE return is inevitable, teases potential reunion with his most iconic rivals CM Punk
articles.summary: WWE veteran Jeff Hardy believes that a return to the company is inevitable before he eventually hangs up his wrestling boots.
articles.body: WWE veteran Jeff Hardy believes that a return to the company is inevitable before he eventually hangs up his wrestling boots. The former WWE Champion has expressed his desire to compete inside a WWE ring again and even teased a potential reunion with one of his most iconic rivals, CM Punk.Hardy has had an iconic wrestling career as both a singles and tag team wrestler, but the TNA Wrestling star isn't ready to call it quits, even though he believes The Hardy Boyz's run could come to an end soon.The 49-year-old star feels he still has several years left in the pro wrestling business. According to reports, the TNA wrestler has since appeared and would be wrestling on a few episodes of "WWE NXT." The veteran star has now discussed a potential return to the TKO-owned promotion. Let’s take a look at his wrestling promotion and the hint about his most iconic rival, CM Punk.WWE legend Jeff Hardy teases potential reunion with CM Punk, wants one more feud with CM Punk in WWEWWE legend Jeff Hardy has recently opened up about his interest in reuniting with WWE before he retires from professional wrestling. He believes that a return to the company is inevitable before he eventually hangs up his wrestling boots. The former WWE Champion has expressed his desire to compete inside a WWE ring again and even teased a potential reunion with one of his most iconic rivals, CM Punk.Hardy discussed his future in professional wrestling during a recent appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet. When asked about his wrestling career, Hardy said he has unfinished business with the company.Speaking with Chris Van Vliet, he stated, "I feel like I will, in a way, [return to WWE]. I feel like it's kind of inevitable that something will happen, whether it be something leading up to the Hall of Fame or whatever, for it to feel right. But yeah, I feel like I have a little more time in a WWE ring before it's all over."Apart from discussing a potential WWE return, Hardy also revealed which opponent he would like to face as his old-time rival if he gets another opportunity with the promotion.Previously, Jeff Hardy and CM Punk had a very famous history, and they had a famous WWE rivalry in 2009 over the World Heavyweight Championship. Jeff Hardy has recently expressed interest in returning to WWE for a potential feud with Punk in 2027. The duo’s last match happened five days later on SmackDown, a steel cage match with Hardy's WWE career on the line.He further added during the interview, "It's hard not to love the feud between Jeff Hardy and CM Punk. When I see him in the WWE universe now, and how good he looks, and how good he's performing, it's like, wow, what would that look like?"Meanwhile, Jeff Hardy further revealed that he has been dealing with bulging discs in his neck and needs to take a few months away from professional wrestling to allow himself to recover.With Hardy still interested in another WWE appearance and a potential reunion with CM Punk, it will be interesting for the fans to watch another memorable rivalry between the two WWE legends.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Suspenden 18 meses al tenista colombiano Daniel Salazar por amaño de partidos y apuestas
articles.standfirst: 138 apuestas y un partido amañado: la sancion al tenista colombiano Daniel Salazar
articles.summary: 138 apuestas y un partido amañado: la sancion al tenista colombiano Daniel Salazar
articles.body: El tenista colombiano Daniel Salazar fue sancionado con 18 meses de suspensión tras admitir irregularidades vinculadas con apuestas y amaño de partidos, según anunció la Agencia Internacional para la Integridad en el Tenis (ITIA). La medida, vigente desde el 11 de noviembre, se extenderá hasta el 10 de mayo de 2028. Salazar, de 25 años y con mejor ranking individual de 648, infringió las normas anticorrupción del tenis al realizar 138 apuestas en partidos entre septiembre de 2020 y septiembre de 2021. Además, la ITIA determinó que, en un torneo del World Tennis Tour de 2024, perdió deliberadamente un juego con su servicio para facilitar apuestas y no reportó un intento de soborno o una propuesta corrupta. La sanción incluye una multa de 10.000 dólares, de los cuales 3.000 quedaron en suspenso. Durante el castigo, el colombiano no podrá competir en eventos organizados o sancionados por World Tennis, la ATP, la WTA, los torneos de Grand Slam ni asociaciones nacionales. La ITIA también informó la suspensión provisional del tenista Mark Vervoort, por negarse a colaborar en una investigación sobre posibles actos de corrupción, incluida su negativa a permitir la inspección de su teléfono móvil. Asimismo, la argentina Valentina Rossi, de 20 años, quedó suspendida provisionalmente tras un presunto positivo por estanozolol en una muestra tomada el 1 de septiembre de 2026 en el World Tennis Tour de Luján. El estanozolol es un esteroide anabólico prohibido en todo momento bajo el Programa Antidopaje del Tenis. Impacto para el tenis colombiano El caso de Salazar representa un golpe para el tenis nacional, pues involucra a un jugador activo del circuito profesional con una sanción por conductas que comprometen la integridad deportiva. La decisión de la ITIA refuerza la política de tolerancia cero frente a apuestas irregulares, amaño de resultados y omisión de denuncias sobre sobornos. La investigación y las sanciones dejan una señal clara: los jugadores deben abstenerse de apostar en tenis, reportar cualquier intento de manipulación y colaborar plenamente con los organismos de integridad.

articles.title: Álvaro Montero no olvida a Millonarios tras ganar la Sudamericana con Boca
articles.standfirst: Álvaro Montero recuerda su paso por Millonarios tras ser campeón de la Copa Sudamericana con Boca Juniors
articles.summary: Álvaro Montero recuerda su paso por Millonarios tras ser campeón de la Copa Sudamericana con Boca Juniors
articles.body: Álvaro Montero vive una de las noches más importantes de su carrera: el arquero colombiano conquistó la Copa Sudamericana con Boca Juniors tras vencer 2-0 a Atlético Mineiro en la final disputada en el estadio Metropolitano de Barranquilla. Sin embargo, en medio de la celebración, el guardameta guajiro recordó con cariño su paso por Millonarios y confirmó que sigue pendiente del equipo azul. La conquista continental representa el primer título internacional de Montero con Boca Juniors. El portero de 31 años fue protagonista en una final que el equipo argentino resolvió con marcador de 2-0 ante Atlético Mineiro, en un estadio Metropolitano de Barranquilla vestido de azul y oro. Además de Sebastián Villa, Montero se sumó al grupo de colombianos que han levantado la Copa Sudamericana con clubes de la región. La consagración también puso fin a una sequía de 18 años de Boca sin títulos internacionales. Tras el partido, cuando le preguntaron si todavía seguía de cerca a Millonarios, Montero no dudó en responder. El arquero aseguró que ve los partidos del equipo bogotano “a cada rato” y dejó claro su afecto por la institución con una frase que rápidamente se hizo viral: “Solo Millos, loca”. Su vínculo con el club capitalino no es casual. Montero defendió la portería de Millonarios durante más de tres años y dejó una huella importante: ganó la Copa Colombia 2022, la Liga I 2023 y la Superliga de Colombia 2024 antes de dar el salto al fútbol argentino Durante la previa de la final, Montero también explicó el origen de una seña que realiza con los dedos en los actos protocolarios de cada partido con Boca. El gesto, que había generado curiosidad en la prensa argentina, nació precisamente durante su etapa en Millonarios. “Es para mi hija, lo creé con la hinchada de Millonarios”, reveló el portero. Según contó, la seña se convirtió en una tradición familiar: sus hijos se la exigen en casa y él la realiza para sentirlos presentes en cada compromiso. Aunque hoy viste la camiseta de Boca Juniors y celebra un título continental, Montero mantiene una conexión especial con Millonarios. El arquero reconoció que sigue los encuentros del equipo albiazul en los cuadrangulares semifinales de la Liga BetPlay, lo que demuestra que su paso por Bogotá dejó una marca profunda. Para los hinchas de Millonarios, la declaración fue una muestra más del cariño que el guardameta conserva por el club que lo consolidó como una de las figuras del fútbol colombiano. Y para Montero, la Copa Sudamericana no solo es una conquista con Boca: también es una victoria que lo conecta con su historia, su familia y una afición que no ha olvidado.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes consoles Trinity Rodman after Kansas City Current end Washington Spirit’s title hopes
articles.summary: Trinity Rodman struggled to hold back her tears after the Washington Spirit lost 2-1 to the Kansas City Current in the 2026 NWSL Championship on Saturday,
articles.body: Trinity Rodman struggled to hold back her tears after the Washington Spirit lost 2-1 to the Kansas City Current in the 2026 NWSL Championship on Saturday, November 21. However, it was Brittany Mahomes, whose team had just won the title, who stopped to comfort the USWNT star. The Kansas City Current co-owner was seen consoling Rodman on the pitch at Audi Field. The defeat was particularly painful for the Spirit forward, who had now lost three consecutive NWSL championship finals with Washington.Brittany Mahomes Shows Support for Trinity Rodman After Kansas City Current's Championship WinMahomes was not on the losing side of the result. She is part of the Kansas City Current's ownership group and had every reason to celebrate the club's first NWSL title. However, she took time to check on Rodman, who was clearly upset after the final whistle. The two were seen sharing a moment on the field as Rodman tried to deal with the result.The loss was not easy for the Washington forward to accept. The Spirit had reached their third consecutive championship game but had failed to win any of them. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 before Gotham FC handed them another 1-0 defeat in 2025. This time, Kansas City stopped them with a 2-1 win.Rodman also had a difficult night physically. She went down in the fifth minute after an aerial challenge involving Kansas City defender Laney Rouse. The forward grabbed her left shoulder and needed medical attention before returning to the game. She continued playing with her shoulder bandaged in the second half.Vanessa DiBernardo gave Kansas City the lead in the 54th minute with a goal directly from a corner kick. The Current then moved closer to the trophy when Debinha scored during stoppage time. Washington still had something to fight for, though.Rodman scored the Spirit's only goal in the 98th minute of the match, heading in a cross from Tara Rudd. However, Washington could not find another goal before the final whistle.After the match, Rodman explained just how much the defeat had affected her."Obviously this one hurts way worse than any of the other ones. I don't even think you have words in this moment, it is too fresh."Her words showed that the result was still difficult to process. Reaching three finals in a row is an achievement, but losing each one has left Washington without the title it has been chasing.Ben Shelton Explains How Trinity Rodman Has Helped His Tennis CareerWhile Rodman was dealing with the disappointment in Washington, her boyfriend Ben Shelton was also experiencing a tough result in Italy. The American tennis player lost to Carlos Alcaraz in the semifinals of the ATP Finals on Saturday.Shelton won the opening set 6-3, but Alcaraz fought back to take the second set 6-3. The Spaniard then won the deciding tiebreak 7-1 to secure a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) victory and move into the final.Shelton has previously spoken about how much Rodman's support means to him. During his run to the US Open final in September, he spoke to ATP Tour about the importance of having a partner who understands the demands of professional sport.He said:"It's very important I think, one, having my family in my corner, who have been super supportive my whole career, it's really important. And, two, having a partner, a girlfriend, who understands all the same things, knows when to support, what to say in tough moments, is selfless enough to be there for me in my moments and actually enjoy my big moments and vice versa, has been really cool. Her path to being a professional athlete and being one of the best soccer players in the world hasn't been easy and she's dealt with more adversity than me."Shelton also recognised that Rodman understands the pressure that comes with competing at the highest level. Her own career has included injury setbacks and difficult periods. She returned to make a strong impact for Washington during the 2026 season.Rodman's 2026 season was also important after she dealt with back and knee injuries in the previous year. She finished the regular season with career highs of 12 goals and eight assists. She also signed a three-year contract extension with Washington in January 2026, which made her the highest-paid women's soccer player in the world.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Just five days until WWE Survivor Series: WarGames, live from Daikin Park in Houston, WWE Raw emanated from Wichita, Kansas with a show headlined by the latest appearance from The Bloodline and a huge Intercontinental Championship defense.
articles.body:
Just five days until WWE Survivor Series: WarGames, live from Daikin Park in Houston, WWE Raw emanated from Wichita, Kansas with a show headlined by the latest appearance from The Bloodline and a huge Intercontinental Championship defense.

What went down on the go-home show before one of the company's biggest premium live events of the year?

Find out the answer to that and more in this recap, featuring grades and analysis for each match and major segment from the November 23 broadcast.

Announced in advance for Monday's show are:

Roman Reigns and The Bloodline appearance

Intercontinental Championship Match: Rey Fenix vs. Ethan Page (c)

Bayley and Stephanie Vaquer vs. Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley

Raw went on the air with 946 attacking Otis and Akira Tozawa to kick off the show, leaving the tandem lying before addressing the fans in Wichita.

Carmelo Hayes told the fans that the Bloodline thrives on comfort, and the 946 are the exact opposite. Lucien Price and Bronco Nima followed with brief bursts on the mic, while Cruz Montana vowed to bring suffering to the Bloodline in Houston.

Keys reminded Roman Reigns that this war of attrition began because he told Jacob Fatu to take him out, that he was not family, just one of the boys.

He offered some final words of warning to the Bloodline to wrap the opening promo up.

This was a fantastic, chaotic, unpredictable way to kick off Raw. This is the type of outside the box booking we need more of, rather than the more polished and formulaic formatting that we typically get from the show.

Montana dropping "s**t" in his promo may get him some heat, but it came across naturally and really added to the sense of danger and uncertainty that surrounded the segment.

Keys looks like a star, Hayes shined, and Jaida Parker getting the "ain't no one safe" line to end the promo plays like she is a bigger part of the act. This has been a fantastic few months for 946 and whatever plans the creative team has for them beyond Survivor Series: WarGames, here's hoping it maintains their momentum.

Intercontinental Championship Match: Rey Fenix vs. "All Ego" Ethan Page

Last Time in Action: Rey Fenix defeated Kit Wilson (SmackDown, November 20); Ethan Page defeated Chad Gable (Raw, November 2)

An excellent match between Rey Fenix and Ethan Page for the latter's Intercontinental Championship was marred by underhanded tactics late, and the heel stealing a win.

Fenix rolled late, using a springboard moonsault to wipe All Ego out on the floor. Back inside the ring, he caught him with a cutter and set him up for the Mexican Muscle Buster.

Always alert, the cunning heel grabbed hold of his opponent's mask, twisted it around his face, then leveled him with a cheap forearm to the back of the head.

An Egoplex and a three-count later, Page retained his title.

Paige defeated Fenix to retain his title

The commentary team of Michael Cole and Corey Graves did a great job of painting the picture of Fenix as a fighting champion. That his booking has supported that makes it that much more effective.

Fenix and Page have incredible in-ring chemistry. Everything looked smooth and easy, even if it was not, a sign that two great wrestlers are locked in.

Page winning cheap, but not illegally, is a great way to present him. He is the smarmy, cunning, conniving heel who can out-think his opponent. Using underhanded tactics without actually cheating is a great way to buy him heat without having to book him similarly to others.

As it turns out, booking Fenix in matches every week is a great way to have at least one outstanding contest on each show.

Team Mexico captain Rey Mysterio hit the ring to reveal the latest and final member of his squad.

The Hall of Famer ran down the lineups for both his team and Team USA at Survivor Series before introducing his final pick...Dominik Mysterio?

Dirty Dom and JD McDonagh interrupted the proceedings, the latter saying he was willing to let bygones be bygones and forgive his father, but only if he adds him to Team Mexico.

The former AAA Mega Champion expressed outrage over the possibility that the fifth participant might be El Grande Americano. He was even more dismayed when the team captain confirmed it, and the reigning AAA Mega Champion joined them in the ring.

Americano revealed that he and Rey would battle Dom and McDonagh right then, right there.

Why have Dom even mention the possibility of El Grande Americano rather than letting the surprise make the moment?

This was fine, but at some point, we need to move Dirty Dom away from his father. They have to stop crossing paths because at this point, it feels like a fail-safe for whenever the creative team doesn't have anything better for the former IC champion to do.

Rey Mysterio and El Grande Americano vs. Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh

Last Time in Action: Rey Mysterio lost to Chad Gable in a match also involving Dragon Lee (Raw, October 19); El Grande Americano, La Parka, and Rey Fenix lost to Los Perros del Mal (AAA, November 14); JD McDonagh and Dominik Mysterio defeated Cruz del Toro and Joaquin Wilde (Main Event, November 11)

Mysterio and Americano defeated The Judgment Day in a hot tag team match that saw Dirty Dom and McDonagh dominate a large portion before losing in the closing moments

Late in the bout, the 2023 Hall of Famer ridded the ring of McDonagh, allowing Americano to level Dom with a headbutt for the win.

A fun, energetic match that highlighted the babyfaces ahead of Survivor Series, against opponents they have history with, it was a perfectly acceptable addition to the show.

Americano and Rey Mysterio defeated Judgment Day

Based on where he is on the card these days, it is almost unfathomable that Dirty Dom was in the most anticipated match of last year's Survivor Series: WarGames event, challenging John Cena for the Intercontinental Championship. It is a testament to him that he remains as over as he is with audiences.

Stateside audiences have not seen Americano wrestle live for months, yet he still drew a huge ovation from the fans in Wichita, which speaks to both the commitment to the character and the impact of AAA.

It took three interruptions, but Cody Rhodes officially announced Seth "Freakin" Rollins as the fifth member of Team USA.

The revelation came moments after CM Punk told his team captain that he was having the time of his life and that he knew the American Nightmare would not let him down. The look on his face as Rhodes introduced Rollins will be etched in the minds of fans, and relived in video packages, for the foreseeable future.

Rollins had an antagonistic smirk on his face as he made his way to the ring, enthusiastic about the negative impact his arrival had on his longtime enemy.

Punk exited the ring, walking out on his team and creating big questions about Team USA's ability to coexist, let alone defeat Team Mexico, at Survivor Series.

"I'm a little worried about CM Punk, Cole. It appears he's gone full Hacksaw Jim Duggan. You never go full Hacksaw," Corey Graves said on commentary.

The look of disappointment and rage that simultaneously painted Punk's, um, painted face upon the Rollins reveal was extraordinary. Facial expressions are key in professional wrestling and the Best in the World proved, again, why that nickname applies.

Kudos to LA Knight for not forgetting that he has issues with Rollins, too, looking anything but pleased as The Visionary stepped into the ring.

In four months, when we are gearing up for Punk vs. Rhodes at WrestleMania, remember this as the moment that sparked that rivalry.

Last Time in Action: Sol Ruca defeated Nikkita Lyons (Main Event, November 11); Lyra Valkyria lost to Lola Vice (Main Event, November 11)

Sol Ruca overcame a bum left knee to defeat a distracted Lyra Valkyria Monday night in a match with Women's Intercontinental Championship implications.

Ruca found herself on the defensive early and often, but capitalized on Valkyria's obsession with Iyo Sky at ringside, seized an opening, and flattened the heel with the Sol Snatcher for the victory.

The commentary team hinted that the win may have earned Ruca a shot at the IC title. If so, could Valkyria be inserted to make it a Triple Threat Match and pay off the tension between her and the champion?

Iyo Sky joined the commentary team for the match following a backstage confrontation with Valkyria. The idea of those two working with each other in an extended program over the IC title is enough for anyone to be excited.

This was Ruca's best performance in a while, though her TV appearances have been few and far between of late. Hopefully, this was a reintroduction to her and the start of a renewed focus on the NXT export.

Valkyria does not get nearly enough credit for being as great as she has been since hitting the main roster. She has completely thrown herself into this heel persona and has done some of her finest work since her turn, even if the creative team has let her down on occasion.

Last Time in Action: Oba Femi defeated Bron Breakker (Raw, November 9)

Following a confrontation in the parking lot earlier in the day with The Vision's Bron Breakker, Austin Theory, and Logan Paul, The Ruler made his way to the ring to address his rivals.

He recalled that the group was meant to be the seeds that formed the true, that bore the fruit of wrestling's future, but no one wants to admit that the tree is dying.

He warned his rivals that the last time he said something would be the end, and he made good on his promise by defeating Brock Lesnar at SummerSlam.

He ended his promo on that note, with no surprise appearance by the heels or predictable sneak attacks to speak of.

Femi is a great speaker. For someone still so early in his career, he has fantastic command of the mic and keeps the fans invested in what he is saying. He rarely stumbles and speaks with a confidence few with his experience would. It is a major reason why he is already at the level he is.

Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley vs. Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley

Last Time in Action: Stephanie Vaquer defeated Jacy Jayne (Raw, November 16); Bayley defeated Michin (Raw, November 9); Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid fought Michin and B-Fab to a No Contest (SmackDown, November 13)

La Primera and The Role Model built momentum for themselves ahead of Saturday's Women's War Games with a hard-fought victory over Fatal Influence.

Not even late-match interference from Women's United States Champion Jacy Jayne could hamper the babyfaces' determination for victory as she was caught cheating, then wiped out by Bayley.

Back inside the ring, Vaquer downed Reid, then delivered the Inferno (modified Spiral Tap) for the win.

A strong match in a string of them tonight, this was a nice showcase for the women's division, even if it was not the strongest sell-job for Saturday's War Games match.

Vaquer and Bayley defeated Reid and Henley

It has been fascinating listening to the commentary team repeatedly refer to Henley as "underrated" because it appears everyone except those who can do anything about it have noticed.

Vaquer is getting back to form after an injury-riddled portion of the year. That bodes well for the women's division as La Primera is one of the best wrestlers on the planet at her best.

Henley and Reid held their own against two of the better workers in the division, never looking out of place. Reid, in particular, has been impressive given her relative inexperience and how quickly she debuted on the main roster.

Roman Reigns showed up with approximately 10 minutes left in the show and, flanked by The Usos, Solo Sikoa, and Jacob Fatu, made his way to the ring to confront Royce Keys and 946 in the show-closing segment.

A brawl erupted, with the heels seemingly getting the better of the babyfaces as Keys sent Reigns into the steel steps. As those two fought around the ring, Keys put The OTC on the announce table, only to eat a big uppercut.

Across the arena, Fatu launched himself over the top rope and onto 946 at ringside, then stood tall as the show went off the air.

The little things: Fatu entered the arena draped in his Samoan Werewolf colors but when the fight erupted, he shed it to reveal the same Bloodline shirt the rest of his family wore. It was a nice moment of unity in which Fatu made it clear he is still his own man, but he is Bloodline when it comes time to battle.

You have to feel happiness for Keys, who is in the biggest storyline of his career, against the top star in the company, and he has shined throughout. He has not allowed the moment to be too big for him. Tonight was another strong effort from the former Powerhouse Hobbs.

Carmelo Hayes as the unhinged member of 946, who is always ready to talk a big game and fight, is a nice touch for him and gives him a personality within the group. That was on full display as he instigated the brawl.

It is appropriate that Punk and Rhodes take home the honors here, having been two of the best parts of the entire build to Survivor Series. Punk's performance was excellent as he expressed excitement and enthusiasm for Team USA, only to have the most fun he has had since returning ripped away from him by the man he trusted not to let him down.

Rhodes' inability to look Punk in the eye as Rollins made his way to the ring was just as good, knowing he had betrayed the trust of someone close to him, even if it was for the right cause.

There is going to be a hell of a WrestleMania program between Punk and Rhodes in the near future and this is going to be one of those moments that we look back on as the emphasis for it. Great stuff all around, with Punk delivering some of the best, stoic, angry facial expressions in recent memory.

This was a banger episode of Raw. Everything hit: the build to Survivor Series: WarGames was great, the in-ring action was above the average television fare, and the hype for Saturday's premium live event headliner was outstanding.

It is unknown yet what SmackDown holds this Friday night, but one would be hard-pressed to imagine a scenario where it comes even close to this go-home broadcast.

articles.title: Seth Rollins Returns as Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, USA's Final Member vs. Mexico at WWE Survivor Series
articles.summary: Seth Rollins was revealed Monday night on Raw as the final member of Team USA ahead of Saturday's WWE Survivor Series premium live event.
articles.body:
Seth Rollins was revealed Monday night on Raw as the final member of Team USA ahead of Saturday's WWE Survivor Series premium live event.

A traditional, five-on-five, elimination match is set for Survivor Series, pitting Team USA against Team Mexico, and Team USA entered Raw in need of one final member.

Co-captains Cody Rhodes and CM Punk had already added Je'Von Evans and LA Knight to the squad, but multiple attempts to find a fifth member last week on SmackDown went awry.

Much to the chagrin of Rhodes, Punk brought out WWE Hall of Famer "Hacksaw" Jim Duggan and offered him a spot on the team, but once Duggan saw a highlight package of Team Mexico's Rey Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee, he quickly declined and left the ring.

Then, United States champion Trick Williams threw his name into the mix, and it looked as though Rhodes and Punk had found their guy.

However, Williams suffered an apparent knee injury during a match against Damian Priest, forcing Rhodes and Punk to go back to the drawing board again.

Near the end of SmackDown, Rhodes finished a phone call and told Punk he believed he had found the final member of Team USA.

When Punk asked who it was, The American Nightmare asked, "How bad do you want to win?"

That led to speculation that Rhodes was speaking to someone Punk had issues with in the past, and that proved to be the case when Rollins was named the fifth member of the team.

Punk and Rollins wrestled each other multiple times in 2025, including Rollins beating Punk and Roman Reigns in a Triple Threat match at WrestleMania 41, and Rollins successfully cashing in his Money in the Bank contract on Punk at SummerSlam.

Rollins has also had his fair share of battles with Rhodes, including multiple singles bouts between them in 2022.

Prior to Monday, Rollins had not been seen on WWE programming since losing to Reigns in the main event of SummerSlam 2026 back in August.

Team USA's need for a fifth member brought him back, though, and he will have to find a way to co-exist with some of his greatest rivals in order to take down Team Mexico.

articles.title: 'I do not see such potential in Gukesh': Belarusian grandmaster Denis Lazavik's brutal verdict ahead of World Championship
articles.summary: Denis Lazavik has made a strong statement ahead of the World Chess Championship 2026, backing Javokhir Sindarov to beat defending champion D Gukesh.
articles.body: Denis Lazavik has made a strong statement ahead of the World Chess Championship 2026, backing Javokhir Sindarov to beat defending champion D Gukesh. The Belarusian grandmaster believes the Uzbek is a clear favourite and does not expect the 14-game contest to be a closely fought battle.Lazavik also questioned Gukesh's potential to become a great world champion, making a particularly hard-hitting remark about the Indian's game and personality."I do not see such potential in Gukesh. Neither in his current play, nor in his general human qualities. So, in this sense, of course, I would like Sindarov to win, establish himself, and continue to be one of the best," Lazavik said in an interview with Chess Plus.'I would not count on any long and equal fight'Lazavik believes Sindarov is in better form and has the ability to control the match. He does not expect the contest to produce a long, closely fought battle.“I would not count on any long and equal fight. If Sindarov had dipped a little recently, then maybe I would have changed my point of view, but he is playing very well. So, I expect the match to unfold without much of a fight. Not a crushing defeat, but something around +1, +2, and Sindarov will hold the edge until the end. Maybe a few games at the end will decide it, but I don’t really believe in that," he said.“So, spectators shouldn’t get their hopes up for a long, drawn-out match, so they won’t be disappointed,” he added.Asked what he personally expected from the contest, Lazavik said he watches chess more as a professional than as a spectator.“I am a professional chess player, so I don’t watch chess for entertainment, it is my profession. When I rest, I prefer to watch something else. If I watch, it is more as a professional, to pick up some ideas," he said.'We need a great Champion, not just on paper'Lazavik also explained why he wants Sindarov to win the title. He believes the Uzbek has the potential to become one of the strongest players in the world and establish himself as a champion who can regularly defend his crown and win tournaments.“But as a spectator, I’d like to see a game played on principle, not strange attempts to put on a show. At the same time, I expect Sindarov to win. He is stronger, and even now his level of play is high enough to become one of the strongest or at least first among equals," Lazavik said.“We need a great Champion, not just on paper, but in reality, who will successfully defend the title and often win tournaments. I see such potential in Sindarov. He plays well and, perhaps, over time will be able to become an example not only for chess players but for other people as well," Lazavik added.Lazavik reiterated his preference for Sindarov, saying he wanted the Uzbek to establish himself among the best players in the world.Gukesh faces stern test against in-form SindarovThe comments come as Gukesh prepares to defend his world title against Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland. The 14-game match begins on November 24 and runs until December 12.Both players are 20 years old, but their preparations for the contest have been very different.Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world champion at 18 in 2024. However, he has struggled to find consistency since that historic achievement and is yet to win a solo classical tournament title after becoming champion. He endured disappointing campaigns at the Prague International Chess Festival, Norway Chess and Chennai Grand Masters in 2026. He also decided to skip the classical legs of the Grand Chess Tour, choosing to play only the rapid and blitz events in Warsaw and Zagreb.The Indian also stayed away from several other major tournaments, including the Freestyle Chess event in Las Vegas, to avoid travel fatigue and focus on his World Championship preparations. His classical rating has slipped to 2710, leaving him 26th in the world rankings. He is also the lowest-ranked reigning world champion in the Elo era.Sindarov, meanwhile, has enjoyed a remarkable year. He became the youngest player to win the FIDE Candidates Tournament on his debut, finishing unbeaten to earn the right to challenge Gukesh. He was also part of Uzbekistan's gold-winning Open team at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, where he won an individual bronze medal.His rise has continued in the rankings. He reached a career-high world No. 4 in classical chess and climbed to No. 2 in the live rapid ratings after winning the 2026 Clutch Chess: Champions Showdown in Saint Louis, USA.Sindarov leads classical head-to-head recordSeveral leading grandmasters have backed Sindarov to dethrone Gukesh. However, the Indian is not paying much attention to the predictions.At the opening press conference, Gukesh made his intentions clear. He said he was not approaching the contest simply as a title defence but wanted to win the world championship all over again.Sindarov, meanwhile, acknowledged the challenge of facing the reigning champion."Compared to the last time I am at a different match, different opponent, different place...surely one of my biggest test. I will try to enjoy the games. Gukesh in 2024 was phenomenal," said Sindarov.The Uzbek also has an advantage in their classical head-to-head record. He leads 2-0, with one draw. Gukesh is yet to beat Sindarov in a classical game.All you need to know about the World Championship matchThe championship will feature 14 classical games. The first player to reach 7.5 points will be crowned world champion. If the scores are level after 14 games, the title will be decided through shorter-format tiebreaks.Both players will get 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, followed by an additional 30 minutes for the rest of the game. A 30-second increment will be added from move 41.To encourage fighting chess, players will not be allowed to agree to a draw before completing 40 moves. Games can still end earlier through threefold repetition or stalemate.The match has a total prize fund of USD 2.5 million. Each decisive victory will be worth USD 200,000, with the remaining prize money divided equally. If the match goes to tiebreaks, the winner will receive USD 1.3 million and the runner-up USD 1.2 million.Gukesh will play with the black pieces in the opening game after drawing the black knight during the colour-allocation ceremony.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
