articles.title: Resurgent J.T. Miller’s ‘grind game’ fueling Rangers’ new identity
articles.summary: His line has consistently delivered the style of play Sullivan wants.
articles.body:
The quotes from J.T. Miller occurred more than two months apart — one on the first day of training camp, the other after falling just short in a measuring-stick game Sunday — but captured just how far the Rangers, and Miller, have already come this season.

After their first on-ice session in September, Miller, off an injury-filled season with just 17 goals and 53 points, said, "I'd like to be better, I want the team to play better, I want better results." The sting from a lost season and public retool still lingered. Miller admitted he learned a lot from his first year as captain and demanded more. And in the aftermath of the Blueshirts' loss to the Hurricanes — the defending Stanley Cup champions, the Metropolitan Division leaders and the ultimate litmus test — on Sunday, Miller, from in front of his locker, said, "I think we've developed a real hate for losing hockey games, which is a good sign of our expectations to one another."

The Rangers' new-look identity, as a checking team who is hard to play against and capable of scoring, has helped them enter the ninth week of the season just outside the playoff cutline based on point percentage. It has helped them take a step forward after two ugly seasons. And at the center of that has been the revival of Miller, who — after a goal and an assist Sunday — has collected six points in the past four games, 12 across the Rangers' last 11 and 19 points for the season while playing with the ideal style for head coach Mike Sullivan's structure.

"He thrives at a grind game," Sullivan said recently of Miller, who's now up to five goals but still has just three at five-on-five. "He's a bull down underneath the hash marks, below the goal line, in behind the net. … When you can use the width of the zone or the depth of the zone, and the way he possesses pucks, he's just tough to handle. He's hard to get it off."

With one more assist, Miller will become just the 184th player in NHL history to reach 500 assists for his career. He might not hit 100 points again like he did with the Canucks in 2023-24. He might never reach the 30-goal threshold for a fourth time in his career, either. But he has become one of the Rangers' most productive and consistent forwards during their recent surge, which includes six wins in their last eight games.

Miller picked up the secondary assist on Mika Zibanejad's power-play goal in the first period against Carolina. Then, with the Rangers scrambling in the third period, Miller fired a shot with the man-advantage that went through traffic and past Brandon Bussi. His individual expected goals of 8.72 and expected goals for percentage of 60.08 both rank second on the Rangers, and Miller, 33, is on pace for the most high-danger scoring chances of his career (120.6), too, according to Natural Stat Trick.

And beyond Tye Kartye, Miller hasn't encountered much consistency with linemates, either. Miller opened the year with the first power-play unit, was demoted to the second group two weeks ago and then returned to the top unit when Dorofeyev sustained an injury. Pavel Dorofeyev, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Alexis Lafrenière, Gabe Perreault and, now, Will Cuylle have all logged multiple games skating alongside the Miller-Kartye duo, and all, for the most part, have controlled play, created scoring chances and limited potential damage from opponents.

"J.T. and Tye we feel have — they've established a certain chemistry that we think is really effective," Sullivan said. "I think J.T.'s grind game is exceptional, and I think Tye helps him in that aspect of it. And then whoever is on that line, I think, becomes a benefactor."

Miller was limited to just 68 games last year and had a pair of stints on injured reserve. The high of winning a gold medal with Team USA at the Winter Olympics was evened out by the lows of the Rangers' campaign, which saw them sink to the bottom of the Eastern Conference.

But, after some limited production and costly turnovers — including a brutal one late in the first period against the Devils last month that led to a goal and the Blueshirts subsequently unraveling — early in the year, Miller has started to find a rhythm. His line has consistently delivered the style of play Sullivan wants. He's on pace for his most points in a year since that 100-point campaign, too.

"We've done a lot of good stuff here lately," Miller said. "… There's a lot to like about the group."

And within those improvements from the Rangers, within the ebbs and the flows of Miller's game, there have been plenty of recent promising strides from their captain, too.

articles.title: Despite Defensive Struggles, Dmitry Orlov Pacing For Best Offensive Season of His Career
articles.summary: The start of the 2026-27 season certainly hasn't gone how Dmitry Orlov has expected. His defensive game as a whole has dropped off significantly since arrivi...
articles.body:
The start of the 2026-27 season certainly hasn't gone how Dmitry Orlov has expected. His defensive game as a whole has dropped off significantly since arriving in San Jose last season and he's certainly been a polarizing player this season in particular. Yet, despite a number of giveaways and poor defensive play, he's pacing for the best offensive season of his career at 35 years of age.

In the first 25 games of the season, Orlov has scored three goals and added 14 assists for a total of 17 points. Over the course of an 84-game season, that puts him on pace for a career-high 57 points. He set his current career-high of 37 points in his first season with the Sharks. Now, of course, while offense from a defenseman is beneficial, that's certainly not all that they should be judged off of.

Orlov is currently third on the Sharks in giveaways with 34, he's on pace to be a -40 by the end of the season. Regardless of the relevance of plus-minus in the modern age of hockey, when it's that egregious, it's notable. According to Dom Luszczyszyn's analytical model, Orlov has a -4.4 defensive rating this season as well.

Simply put, Orlov has been massively ineffective in his own end to start the season but he's one of the few Sharks putting points on the board. After his three assist performance against the Seattle Kraken, he's also sitting on 299 career assists.

The question remains, is Orlov's offensive contribution enough to offset his defensive lapses or will the Sharks eventually need to find a way to get more stability on their blue line if they want to push for the playoffs this spring?

articles.title: Lakers optimistic about Austin Reaves’ availability after star guard’s latest step
articles.summary: Austin Reaves’ took an important step in his return-to-play process
articles.body:
But he also took an important step in his return-to-play process before the Lakers hosted the Jazz again at Crypto.com Arena, leaving the team optimistic about his availability to return later in the week.

Reaves participated in a "stay-ready" game on Monday after the team's shootaround at their practice facility as he recovers from his bruised left heel.

The star guard was a full participant in Sunday's practice , but it didn't include any live action.

The Lakers ruled him out for Monday's game Sunday evening after coach JJ Redick said Reaves was "making progress."

"We want to be consistent with our [return-to-play] stuff," Redick said. "I think [Monday] was a big step just in terms of getting a stay-ready game in. And he played great, moved great. We're optimistic for the rest of this week going forward."

The 28-year-old guard suffered the injury on Nov. 11 and has been considered day-to-day since.

The Lakers' next game after Monday is against the Spurs on Friday in San Antonio.

Reaves has averaged 24.7 points (51.3% from the field, 40.9% from beyond the arc), 4.7 assists and 3.3 rebounds in the 12 games he's played.

articles.title: Chris Simms shares his thoughts on the Browns, Deshaun Watson
articles.summary: The former veteran quarterback added his two cents on the state of the Browns and Deshaun Watson.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are in a good spot. They control their own playoff destiny and could even win their division if things break right in the second half of the year. At this moment, it's hard to see this team not making the postseason.

Even more encouraging, their starting quarterback just played his best game in years. Deshaun Watson threw for 312 yards and rushed for another 49 in a comeback win against the Houston Texans last week. It was easily the best the offense has looked all year.

Watson's time with the Browns has been nothing less than horrific. There has been more talk about his behavior on the field than what he was doing on the field, which was also very bad. So the idea that he might finally be turning a corner in his fifth year in Cleveland is both exciting and shocking.

However, one game does not qualify as turning a corner. It could very well be a one off fluke. Regardless, it was great to see that he still had that level of play in him and that he could actually lead this Browns offense in meaningful games.

Last week, Chris Simms of NBC Sports had thoughts about Watson and what his current level of play might mean for the Browns moving forward.

"I would even say if they don't make the playoffs and he continues to play the way he is, and kind of still looking the way he's been looking here, I think that'll probably be enough for him to stay there, too."

This is where some are going to want to put on the brakes.

If you are planning to re-sign Watson, then I question what your long-term goals are. It just doesn't make sense to extend an injury-prone quarterback as he enters his early 30s when he has played one good game in five years.

The only way that it makes sense to me is on a one-year bridge deal as the franchise brings along a high draft pick slowly and not force that rookie into action. Turn Watson into what the Las Vegas Raiders did with Kirk Cousins; start for half the year before turning things over to the rookie. But if you are looking for a long term answer at quarterback then a significant commitment to Watson just doesn't make sense.

LAHINA, Hawaii (AP) — Collin Chandler scored 21 of his game-high 24 points in the second half and No. 19 BYU held off Washington 83-77 Monday on the opening day of the Maui Invitational.

The Cougars (6-0) trailed by as many as 15 points in the first half before rallying and turning back the Huskies (4-1).

BYU took the lead for good with 5:49 to play on a free throw by Bruce Branch III. After Washington cut it to 66-65 on a jumper by Ryan Beasley, the Cougars answered with an inside bucket by Jaxon Kohler that spurred an 11-4 run that Chandler punctuated with a pair of free throws. That gave BYU its largest lead of the game at 77-69 with 34 seconds remaining.

Chandler shot 6 of 12 from the field, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range and was 9 of 10 from the free throw line.

Kohler scored 15 points, Tyler Betsey had 13 and Branch 10 for the Cougars, who shot 59.3% (16 of 27) in the second half.

LeJuan Watts scored 21 points, Beasley had 20 and Lathan Sommerville chipped in 13 points and nine rebounds for the Huskies.

Washington led 29-14 with 8:57 left in the first half after a pair of Beasley free throws.

BYU made just 22 of its 36 attempts from the free throw line, while Washington was 23 of 27 from the line.

The Huskies drained their first two attempts from beyond the arc — both by Steele Venters — but made only two of their final 16 from distance.

BYU played its second straight game without leading scorer Robert Wright III (24.3 points per game).

articles.title: Joel Klatt explains why Michigan football's UCLA upset wasn't a shock
articles.summary: Joel Klatt explains why Michigan's defense deserves national recognition for continuing to excel despite getting little help from the offense.
articles.body:
Michigan football shocked much of the country by beating the previously undefeated UCLA team that came into Ann Arbor this past Saturday. But one person who wasn't shocked? Joel Klatt.

Fox Sports' premier college football color commentator couldn't even feign shock, because as moribund as the Michigan offense has been all year, the defense has been stellar. And given what he's seen from the Wolverines on that side of the ball, it gives them a chance in every game, no matter the opponent.

"That Michigan defense is one of the best things anybody does in college football. That is an elite defense," Klatt said. "And that's why it was always going to be a difficult task for UCLA to go in there and win this game on the road. That Michigan defense is outstanding. I think [it's] one of the best defenses in the country.

"And it's not just statistically the best defenses, because you've got to put in level of competition and what can they do? How do they cover? How physical are they? How good are they against the run? How good are they against the pass? Can they get after the passer? How complementary are they? And here's where I land. I think the best defenses in America come from this group: Georgia , Michigan, Tennessee , Texas , Notre Dame , probably Iowa and UCLA . Those are the best defenses in America right now."

What might be surprising then is that Michigan won the game with one of the worst offenses in the country. As Klatt notes, the Bruins have one of the elite defenses at the moment. And yet, it was the Wolverines who prevailed.

So, as Klatt sees it, no matter the ease that UCLA was going to find at The Big House in terms of facing the Michigan offense, it was the Michigan defense that was poised to give it fits. And give it fits it did, as the Bruins only got into the end zone once -- with 10 seconds remaining in regulation.

"You might be surprised about UCLA, but they're actually leading the country in yards per play defense. That's what I think is the best metric: You snap the football, how many yards do you give up on a per-snap basis? UCLA actually leads the country in that. As for the ability to create havoc in man coverage and all that, probably Georgia. Michigan and Notre Dame, Tennessee and Texas rush the passer as well as anyone. Tennessee is outstanding.

"So this was always going to be a difficult game for UCLA, and it comes right down to the wire. Why? Because of the defense for Michigan. And by the way, they have just stood on their head the entire season with no help, no help. I give them a lot of credit because they don't seem to have imploded on the defensive side. They don't seem to care all that much that nothing is happening on the opposite side of the ball for them. They just go out there and continually play hard.

"So credit to Jay Hill, their defensive coordinator, and Kyle as the head coach, and everything they've got going from a culture standpoint on that defensive side of the football, because they're excellent on that side. And they were always going to make life difficult for UCLA."

Perhaps this was a good challenge for the maize and blue to overcome, as they finish out with a road trip to Ohio State this upcoming Saturday.

articles.title: Allen Graves Reveals "Best Advice" Given Before Career Night Against Pistons
articles.summary: The rookie earned his first starting nod with key players out due to injury, and he certainly made the most of his opportunity.
articles.body:
Looking back at the Toronto Raptors ' standout 105-102 win over the Detroit Pistons, rookie first-round pick Allen Graves truly was unbelievable. In his first career start, the former Santa Clara Bronco contributed 20 points, 10 rebounds, three steals, and a block on 6-for-9 shooting.

With key injuries to Kawhi Leonard (knee), RJ Barrett (hamstring), and Collin Murray-Boyles (concussion), it was obvious that Scottie Barnes wouldn't be able to take over alone against a vicious Pistons defense. Many expected it to be Immanuel Quickley or Ja'Kobe Walter providing the majority of the secondary scoring, but Graves proved to be the best second fiddle available to Barnes on both ends of the floor.

When talking to the 2026 No. 19 pick, the media asked Graves what the best advice he has been given was; his answer was evident in his stellar play.

"[The advice was] to just be myself, be confident out there," said Graves. "Earlier on in the season, it was definitely me just doing a lot of thinking, in my head, trying not to make a mistake, trying to be the perfect player, but in reality, I'm never going to be the perfect player. I'm always going to make mistakes, and just being willing to go out there and make them, and grow and learn because, like I said, that's how I learn, that's how I grow from it. Just being able to go out there and be confident in myself and the player that I am, and know that I belong here."

It hasn't been entirely evident that he has been playing with little confidence, but now that he has switched up his approach, it's apparent that he has figured it out. Even in such a stacked draft class, rookies need time to find their footing in the league, and the Raptors should be thrilled that it only took 16 games for their newest piece to make his name known.

While Leonard and Barrett continue to make progress towards returning to action, there really is no better time for Graves to keep being aggressive offensively. The lack of offensive consistency around Barnes has been an issue for the past year and a half, so if Graves can prove that he can find his own shot regularly, Toronto truly may have found a diamond in the rough. He was selected largely because of his exceptional two-way ability, a typical prototype for a Raptors prospect, but he has consistently made winning plays that don't necessarily show up in the stat sheet. If he is able to add the two together moving forward, he could add some much-needed help to a severely lacking second unit.

At the end of the day, consistency is going to be key for the entire Raptors team. They were considered to be a dark horse contender to win the NBA championship this season because of the several scoring options alongside Leonard and Barnes, matched with a defense suited to be the best in the league. With injuries plaguing the early portion of their season so far, the only consistency from the entire roster has come from Barnes. This was evident throughout Toronto's six-game losing streak prior to the win in Detroit, specifically when looking at the constant scoring droughts that led to giving up four double-digit leads.

articles.title: SEC threatening vote on LSU expulsion for a second time after RJ Luis drama
articles.summary: It’s the latest twist in the saga between the conference and the school.
articles.body:
The SEC is planning to meet on Dec. 3 in order to "decide whether to terminate LSU as an SEC member institution," the conference revealed on Monday in a legal filing in federal court in Alabama, upping the ante in its ongoing battle with the school.

It's the latest twist in the saga between the conference and the school following LSU's decision to roster RJ Luis Jr. last week in defiance of the SEC's rule prohibiting anyone who has signed a pro contract from playing for one of its members' athletic programs.

The conference filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against LSU on Monday, revealing plans to consider terminating the school's membership.

A statement from the SEC read: "The Southeastern Conference on Monday filed an amended complaint and motion for temporary restraining order in its federal lawsuit against Louisiana State University stating that the presidents and chancellors of the SEC will meet on Thursday, December 3, to deliberate LSU's ongoing membership in the Conference."

"The lawsuit seeks to protect the Conference's ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the statement continued. "The Conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs. Monday's filing advances the Conference's obligation to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities."

According to conference rules, at least two-thirds of the 15 other member school presidents would need to vote to terminate LSU's membership.

LSU has not publicly responded to the conference's move.

This is the second time that the SEC has threatened to hold a vote on LSU's membership, with the first instance coming in a September amended federal complaint stemming from an attempt by LSU's football team to roster tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, both of whom had signed NFL contracts and participated in training camps.

LSU football coach Lane Kiffin eventually backed off and the vote never took place.

In the new filing on Monday, the SEC alleged that LSU had "planned to roster Mr. Luis all along and that they have been working with Mr. Luis and his counsel to use the Luis [lawsuit] to achieve that result while simultaneously representing to the SEC that Mr. Luis would not take the court for LSU—all as part of an effort to delay and ultimately block consideration by the CEOs of potential expulsion of LSU from the Conference."

LSU basketball coach Will Wade rostered Luis, a St. John's player during the 2024-25 season, on Nov. 17 and the following day he took the court against UL Monroe despite "numerous representations" ahead of the game that he would not play, the SEC alleged in its filing.

Luis' legal team had tried to hold SEC commissioner Greg Sankey and the conference in contempt of a state court order that prevented the conference from punishing LSU if it tried to roster or play the ex-Red Storm player.

Luis decided to leave LSU following a statement from school president Wade Rousse that he had told Wade not to play Luis.

The court filing on Monday said that the "SEC has no avenue to penalize LSU" and suggested that a "forced association" with LSU "violates the Conference's fundamental First Amendment rights."

The conference also called LSU's actions "antithetical to the SEC's mission and core values."

articles.title: What police report says about Andrew Marsh's indecent exposure charge
articles.summary: Andrew Marsh, who leads Michigan football in receptions, was suspended for one game after allegedly exposing himself to a female delivery driver.
articles.body:
Michigan football is expected to get starting receiver Andrew Marsh back to play against Ohio State on Saturday, Nov. 28, after he served a one-game suspension in last week's upset of then-No. 4 UCLA.

Marsh was suspended for allegedly exposing himself to a woman delivering an order from McDonald's in February, something for which he still faces a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure.

However, the sophomore denied he did so intentionally, according to a police report obtained by the Free Press on Monday, Nov. 23. Marsh was also accused in the report of making romantic advances toward the driver via DoorDash chat.

Washtenaw County prosecutors issued a misdemeanor indecent exposure complaint against the 19-year-old Marsh in October, court records show, and he is due in Washtenaw District Court 14A for a pre-trial hearing on Dec. 2. An indecent exposure charge is punishable by up to a year in prison and up to $1,000 fine, or both.

Hours before the Free Press received the report from the the Pittsfield Department of Public Safety, coach Kyle Whittingham explained why Marsh was suspended Saturday.

"After gathering information and doing research, it was my decision [to suspend him]," Whittingham said. "Didn't put that in the hands of the team. That was the decision I made to sit Andrew out last week."

Per the report, Marsh requested the food be delivered to him in person, at which point he allegedly answered the door wearing a U-M blanket.

"When [Marsh] answered the door, she advised he had a University of Michigan fleece blanket draped over his shoulders and that she saw the side of his hip and believed he was unclothed under the blanket," the report states. "She quickly delivered the food and turned to leave when he asked if extra ketchup was added to the order.

"[She] said when she turned to face him again, the blanket was pulled apart exposing his penis to her. She confirmed that she did in fact observe his penis."

The driver told police she "quickly left and shortly after, received a message via the DoorDash app advising her that she was attractive and could return to his address."

"You looked good too," Marsh allegedly typed, according to a screenshot of a DoorDash chat included in the report. "Come back if you onnat."

The driver then received another DoorDash order to the same neighborhood, she told police, but clarified she could only see the address if she accepted the order − she declined, concerned it was the same as before. Two officers went to Marsh's home and interviewed him and he "stated he lives alone and wasn't sure why we were there," an officer wrote in the report.

When the officer asked him what happened with the DoorDash driver, "he admitted to sending text messages to her telling her that she was cute and advised that he had put in another DoorDash order shortly after," per the report.

Marsh also stated he "hadn't intentionally exposed his genitals to her." The officer told him not to send any more messages to her and told Marsh "she was deeply uncomfortable by what had transpired."

Whittingham said Monday that the Wolverines were informed of the situation on Thursday and he met with Marsh to inform him of the suspension. Whittingham called it "unfortunate" and "bad judgment" when asked about it on Saturday, but said he couldn't speak directly to the specifics.

PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Deni Avdija scored 31 points and hit five of Portland's 19 3-pointers to lead the Trail Blazers to a 128-111 win over the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday night.

The Trail Blazers crushed the Sixers all game with the long ball and handed them just their fourth loss of the season.

Donovan Clingan had 15 points and 18 rebounds for Portland. Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday each scored 18 points. Holiday made four 3s.

Avdija was 4 of 4 on 3s and had already scored 22 points with 6:03 left in the first half just one game after Milwaukee's Tyler Herro scored 50 against Philadelphia. Avdija, the 25-year-old from Israel, had pockets fans that were scattered throughout the lower bowl of the arena chant his name and sing over the final minutes.

Avdija acknowledged fans after the game with an appreciative wave and blew kisses to them as he walked to the locker room.

Scoot Henderson and Holiday hit consecutive 3s in the third that ran Portland's lead to 96-87 and Jayson Kent hit the team's 16th 3 to close the quarter with a 101-92 lead.

The Trail Blazers finished 3-3 on the six-game road trip that included losses on consecutive nights to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

LeBron James scored 23 points, his most yet in a game in his first season with the 76ers. He hit his first four 3s of the game while the rest of the Sixers were just 4 of 23.

The Sixers shot just 9 of 33 on 3-point attempts.

Jaylen Brown scored 20 points in his return from a two-game absence with a hamstring injury and Tyrese Maxey added 22. Joel Embiid (illness) did not play for the Sixers who saw a five-game win streak come to an end.

Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori got the win with his son Dante, a Phillies minor league prospect, watching courtside with Phillies general manager Preston Mattingly.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham praises Michigan's freshman standouts in UCLA upset
articles.summary: Kyle Whittingham highlights Michigan's emerging freshman talent, Marky Walbridge's bright future and the importance of enrolling early.
articles.body:
Generally, the best teams, the teams that win tough games, are the ones that have a lot of veteran leadership. Though Michigan football had a lot of returning talent from last year, it's still one of the younger teams in the Big Ten.

And on Saturday against UCLA , it was even younger.

The Wolverines ended up starting an astounding five true freshmen on offense, to go along with sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood and offensive lineman Avery Gach. With running back Savion Hiter, right tackle Marky Walbridge, wide receivers Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson, and tight end Mason Bonner, the maize and blue had a bit of a youth movement going on in Ann Arbor.

And they walked away with an 18-16 triple overtime victory against then-undefeated UCLA.

Head coach Kyle Whittingham broke it down with Jon Jansen on the Inside Michigan Football radio show on Monday night.

"The point of emphasis was, hey, you guys all have a great opportunity to be major contributors, and you're all going to play big roles, and you need to be ready for the moment," Whittingham said. "And they certainly were."

Photos: Michigan football celebrates Senior Day with win over UCLA

It wasn't just that Michigan started all kinds of first-year players; it's that all contributed. Whittingham was pleased to see that they all were contributing factors in such a pivotal game.

"Savion Hiter had a big day, over 100 yards rushing," Whittingham said. "Bonner made three critical catches, the one in the end zone. That was a tough catch. That was contested, and he was able to come away with that ball, and that was outstanding. Then the receivers, Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson, contributed as well. And the right tackle, Marky Walbridge, for a freshman, is just on his way to having a great career here at Michigan. I believe he's got a very bright future. And they didn't play perfect, but you talk about a guy that was thrust into a situation and the way he responded, couldn't be more proud of him."

As for Hiter, Moa, and Johnson, the expectation was that they would play early, then the question became just how impactful they were going to be. But Walbridge? He wasn't supposed to see the field in his freshman campaign.

With the offensive line having lost both starting offensive tackles -- Blake Frazier and Andrew Sprague -- Walbridge has played out of necessity.

There's still a lot of literal growth that Whittingham says Walbridge needs to become the player he will eventually become, but he's already starting to show signs of just how good he might be.

"He has all the basics and all the fundamentals that you need to be a top-notch offensive tackle," Whittingham said. "He's got to put on some weight and strength. That's got to happen and it will. He's a tireless worker in the weight room and he made great strides since January when he first got here. This offseason will be big for Marky and if he can make those same strides again and get himself to that next level, then he's going to be a force to be reckoned with."

Walbridge did grade out poorly per PFF, which had him as the dead-last Wolverine to take the field on offense. But he's showing signs of holding up.

And he's gotten the opportunity because he arrived on campus early -- four of the five who started had. And Whittingham believes that the players who arrive in January have a massive leg up on those who come in June. The only freshmen who've been regular contributors who were June arrivals are Mason Bonner and edge rusher Tariq Boney.

"It's a huge point of emphasis," Whittingham said. "The percentages are way in favor of guys going that route and being able to graduate early. Probably 80, maybe close to 90% of the freshmen that are coming out of high school and into a college program have the early graduation track that they're on. It's such a big advantage in so many aspects. You get a whole semester of academics under your belt. You get a whole weightlifting cycle, a spring ball. You get to learn the complete offense or defense as the case may be. Then you go home for May for your break and come back. It's like you're a veteran in June when you come back. Rather than the old school come in June, and you're trying to figure out what's going on, and even all during fall camp, it's all brand new to you. Such an advantage to play early. You almost have to be an early graduate. It's not 100%, but it sure gives you a huge leg up in that regard."

We'll see how much action the aforementioned five get this week in the big showdown at Ohio State .

articles.title: What Did I Just Watch: Marquette 61, Milwaukee 57
articles.summary: I swear that the Golden Eagles had multiple double digit leads but had to sweat out a finish against the Panthers.
articles.body:
Because sometimes that's how life works sometimes, I didn't get home and get the TV on for Marquette's 6pm start against Milwaukee at the Klosche Center until after the first quarter ended. What did I miss? I missed the Golden Eagles rattling off a 20-3 run to take a 22-9 lead with 49 seconds left in the opening period. That included a 14-0 run after Milwaukee took what would become their final lead of the game at 9-8. Amina Traore was ripping the Panthers apart nearly by herself, hitting all five of her first quarter shots plus grabbing a rebound and dishing two assists on the 6 buckets that she didn't score herself. She also had a block and a steal for an absolutely ridiculous nine minutes of action in the first frame.

The second quarter started with Marquette up 22-13 after the Panthers scored the last four points of the quarter…. and then Milwaukee put together a 12-4 run to open the second quarter. So, that's 16-4 in favor of the home team, and TA-DA, Marquette's margin was down to just one point, 26-25.

The Panthers still didn't have an answer for Traore, and she scored six points in the final 2:30 before halftime to put Marquette up seven going into the break, 32-25. The Golden Eagles spent the third quarter slowly pushing the Panthers away from them. Up 9, up 11, then after Milwaukee got it within six with 3 and change to play, MU scored the next six to stake themselves to a 12 point lead. Even with Traore racking up three fouls in the first five minutes of the quarter — her first three of the game — Marquette seemed to get along without her for a moment, and she even slipped back into the game to score the bucket that had the Golden Eagles up 12, 48-36.

Ten straight for Milwaukee. Two free throws to end the third, then eight straight to open the fourth. Two point game. A layup from Izzy Pugh got Milwaukee within one. Another one just after the clock went under five to play, back to a one point game. Bad times, but Marquette answered. MacKenzie Givens got a pair of buckets on either sid of a Brooklyn Hall jumper for six in a row and it's a seven point game, 57-50, with 2:27 left. Cool. Good great fun, just close the door…..

Five straight for Milwaukee in just over a minute, and now it's a two point game with 78 seconds left. Great. Oh, and Traore just fouled out, too. Perfect.

On the other end, Kinley Asp drives, then turns around to kick out to the open shooter that rotated into the spot Asp left…. except the shooter is Kayl Petersen who is 0-5 from distance in this game and 4-for-21 on the year before this contest tipped off. She misses. Hall comes up with a steal on the other end, and we're under 30 seconds left. Asp makes her two freebies after Milwaukee fouled, and we're in this loop until the end when Marquette finally wins, 61-57.

What an absolute mess. Marquette lost the part of the game that I watched by a score of 44-39. Milwaukee was Not Good, but their 8-for-24 three-point shooting has MU's 0-for-10 beat pretty easily, so you see how they managed to stay right with the Golden Eagles once UWM shook off that early run.

Amina Traore's 22 points leads Marquette here, as the Golden Eagles played without Halle Vice once again. She also added three rebounds, a block, and two steals. Kayl Petersen was 0-for-6 behind the arc but 5-for-8 inside it, and she had nine rebounds and four assists to lead MU in both categories.

Up Next: Marquette heads to the Bahamas for Thanksgiving, which is nice. Playing #20 Illinois on Friday at 10am Central time on FloSports? Well, that's probably less fun, given how this went. Marquette's second game of the Baha Mar event is on Sunday, and they'll face Belmont for that one. The Illini are 4-0 after beating Ball State by 40 last Wednesday, while the Bruins are going to be 1-6 when this 83-39 fourth quarter score against LSU comes to an end in about seven minutes of game time.

articles.title: Lions Thanksgiving Injury Report Includes Several Concerning Names
articles.summary: Four Detroit Lions defenders were listed as non-participants Monday, while Sam LaPorta was limited ahead of Thanksgiving against Chicago.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions have released their initial injury report ahead of Thursday's massive Thanksgiving Day showdown against the Chicago Bears, and there are several names worth monitoring.

Coming off Sunday's 31-21 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Lions (8-2) have a short turnaround before hosting the Bears (8-2) at Ford Field. According to the team's official injury report , four defensive players were listed as non-participants Monday, while tight end Sam LaPorta was limited.

Detroit Lions Initial Thanksgiving Day Injury Report

The Lions conducted a walkthrough Monday. All practice participation designations are estimates rather than results from a full practice.

The biggest concern from Monday's report is that all four non-participants play defense, including Chuck Clark and DJ Wonnum. Both contributed to Sunday's victory over Tampa Bay, making their availability especially important with another game just days away.

On the positive side, D.J. Reed was listed as a full participant despite his hip injury. That's encouraging news for a Detroit secondary that recently received another positive update regarding Kerby Joseph .

Sam LaPorta's ankle injury is also worth watching, although his estimated limited participation is more encouraging than a non-participation designation. Detroit will continue evaluating its injured players as the week progresses.

The Lions are coming off a game in which they had several injury concerns entering the matchup , and this quick turnaround only adds to the challenge.

Detroit and Chicago will kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Thanksgiving Day, November 26 , with the game televised nationally on CBS. With both teams entering at 8-2, the health of Detroit's roster could play an important role in the NFC North showdown.

articles.title: Bill Simmons believes JJ McCarthy is following Eli Manning blueprint with Giants
articles.summary: JJ McCarthy might not be putting up video-game numbers, and his erratic play remains a question mark, but he is checking the right boxes in his first year wi...
articles.body:
JJ McCarthy might not be putting up video-game numbers, and his erratic play remains a question mark, but he is checking the right boxes in his first year with the New York Giants , helping them string up a 6-3-1 record.

On Sunday, the Giants notched their third win in four games after beating the Jacksonville Jaguars, 23-18 , at MetLife Stadium. McCarthy went 18-of-38 for 173 yards, one touchdown, and zero interceptions. He added seven carries for 33 yards. He also made a key pass to Malachi Fields in the fourth quarter, practically sealing the hard-earned victory.

For The Ringer's Bill Simmons , McCarthy is following a familiar template in New York.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"They're back. This is the Eli Manning blueprint, where it's like, 'Throw the throw! I have no idea if this guy's good or not,'" said Simmons on his podcast.

"There's something safe about him even though he's making mistakes. But I just feel like they should give JJ Eli's old number. His stats are never that good. You kind of can't remember five great plays that he made, but you remember that one awesome run and that one awesome scramble, and the other team's fans and defense can't believe they didn't get him for five more sacks and two picks."

Manning led the Giants to two titles and became a two-time Super Bowl MVP. Clearly, McCarthy has a long way to go to reach the same level. But if he continues to build his confidence, sharpen his decision-making, and develop a winning mentality that defined Manning's tenure, he could carve out a similar legacy.

Simmons added that McCarthy has helped the Giants find "an identity," which was in full display against the Jaguars, after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

"They missed a 32-yard field, (Cam) Skattebo fumbled, and McCarthy had two bombs where the guy was wide open, and he just overthrew him. Even with all that happened, they were in control of the whole game," said Simmons.

The Giants will visit the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

articles.title: Hellebuyck returns to form, making 19 saves as the Devils beat the Blue Jackets 3-2
articles.summary: (AP) — Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves two days after getting an early hook and the New Jersey Devils beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 3-2 Monday night.Hellebu...
articles.body:
NEWARK, N.J. (AP) — Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves two days after getting an early hook and the New Jersey Devils beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 3-2 Monday night.

Hellebuyck was lifted a little more than nine minutes into a 9-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner and 2025 NHL MVP gave up four goals on six shots before being removed from the game.

Timo Meier, Brenden Dillon and Connor Brown scored for the Devils, who are 10-3-0 at home this season.

The Blue Jackets scored late in the first and second periods with goals by Charlie Coyle and Mikael Pyyhtia.

Dillon gave New Jersey a 2-0 lead at 8:12 in the first period when he caught a puck off the draw at the point and shot past goalie Cam Talbot. It was the defenseman's first goal since Nov. 28, 2025.

With 2:41 left in the period, the Devils turned the puck over in the offensive zone and Zach Werenski found Coyle for the goal, cutting the New Jersey lead in half.

Brown made it 3-1 at 14:41 in the second, only for Pyyhtia to make it 3-2 with a short-handed goal a little over five minutes later.

Hellebuyck was the difference-maker, turning aside another short-handed attempt early in the third. The Devils faced heavy pressure, forced to ice the puck before defenseman Declan Chisholm took a cross-checking penalty at 11:09, giving Columbus a power play that New Jersey killed off.

Talbot was pulled for the extra attacker in the final two minutes, but the Devils held on for the win. Talbot stopped 27 shots.

Columbus forward Mathieu Olivier left the game with an upper-body injury in the second period and did not return.

The Blue Jackets and Devils play the second half of a home-and-home series Wednesday night in Columbus.

"I think it's possible. Today was a big day for me, getting over that hump with the injury, as far my running, my position work, I felt explosive, felt pretty good. It was one of those days where I took a big leap," the Lions corner said, via Will Burchfield of 97.1 The Ticket.
